Kind: manual

Decision to record: "Decisions with Receipts" becomes Liminal's headline on every external surface.

Context: On 2026-10-05 the founder ruled that every external Liminal surface leads with "Decisions with receipts" (founder-brain decision record, merged as PR #1113). Until now the public surfaces led with a description of the product. The new headline names what Liminal proves: a decision is read by agents, corrected by a person, ratified, and saved as a record signed on the device, which anyone can verify offline.

What it commits us to: every external claim should point at a signed, independently verifiable record rather than a promise. The first public receipt will be this decision itself, exported as a proof bundle with its offline verifier, and published only after the founder has reviewed it.

Open questions: which surface switches first, the front door or the deck; and how to show a receipt without asking a visitor to run a terminal command.
packet.user_correction: The Analyst is right that the headline and the proof must not drift apart, but the gate it asks for is already part of the ruling. The decision binds every use with truth guards: "receipts" means the record Liminal produces today, signed on the device, hash-linked and checkable offline, never enforcement; and until the tamper test is recorded as passed in our claim ledger, a public surface says only what is shown. Surfaces switch one at a time, each with my sign-off, not all at once. What the read missed is that the receipt is not future infrastructure: the offline verifier already runs and fails loudly on a one-byte change. What is still ahead is making it checkable without a terminal, and the "goal" link of the chain, which is direction, not product.

reads.hidden_risk: The brand claim creates a self-referential accountability loop: the headline promises verifiable receipts, so any external surface that goes live *before* a verifiable receipt exists is immediately in contradiction with the claim. Sequencing and proof-bundle readiness are therefore coupled to brand credibility in a way that is not yet acknowledged.
reads.next_move: Ask: What is the minimum viable receipt format that a non-technical visitor can verify without a terminal command, and what is the concrete completion criterion for 'founder has reviewed it' — deadline, checklist, or sign-off artifact?
reads.quoted: every external claim should point at a signed, independently verifiable record
reads.situation: A brand pivot has been ratified: the headline shifts from product description to proof-of-process claim ('Decisions with receipts'). Two variables are currently collapsed into one decision: (1) which surface changes first (sequencing), and (2) how the receipt is made legible to non-technical visitors (UX/accessibility). These are independent problems being treated as one rollout question. Additionally, the first public proof bundle is gated on founder review but no review timeline or criteria are specified, creating a potential bottleneck between commitment and execution.

reads.hidden_risk: Outreach sent before the first receipt is published could reference a claim ('anyone can verify offline') that has no live artifact yet, undermining the credibility the headline is designed to establish.
reads.next_move: Identify one warm prospect or press contact who has expressed interest in verifiable AI audit trails; draft a one-sentence cold note on a single channel (email) with the smallest ask: a 15-minute call timed to coincide with the receipt bundle going live, so the outreach lands with a working proof link rather than a promise.
reads.situation: Liminal has adopted a new headline — 'Decisions with receipts' — across all external surfaces, replacing product-description copy. The first public receipt (this decision itself) is pending founder review before publish. Two surfaces are in contention for first switch: the front door (website) and the pitch deck. The proof bundle also needs a non-terminal UX for visitors.

reads.hidden_risk: The framing is performatively circular: the decision record is being treated as a receipt before the receipt mechanism actually exists in a form any external party can verify. Calling the PR merge itself a 'signed, independently verifiable record' overclaims — PR #1113 is an internal artifact, not a cryptographically signed proof bundle with a shipped offline verifier. The Analyst likely accepted this framing at face value, praising the commitment without flagging that the proof infrastructure is still hypothetical ('published only after the founder has reviewed it' — i.e., not yet published). The brand promise therefore runs ahead of the technical reality by at least one full release cycle.
reads.next_move: Require that the proof bundle and offline verifier be demonstrably functional and publicly accessible before any external surface carries the headline. Otherwise the first thing a skeptical visitor discovers is that 'Decisions with receipts' is itself a receipt-free claim — exactly the reputational failure the brand is designed to prevent.
reads.quoted: The first public receipt will be this decision itself
reads.situation: A founder has declared a new brand headline ('Decisions with receipts') and framed the announcement itself as the inaugural proof of that claim — a self-referential gesture that conflates intention with evidence.
